newsitem.title: USA: Tennessee karnal bunt in small area, low level - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Tennessee karnal bunt in small area, low level - USDA.

text.p: The karnal bunt wheat fungus detected in some soft red winter wheat growing areas of Tennessee has been at very low levels and only in small areas, said the Agriculture Department official in charge of USDA's karnal bunt eradication efforts.

"We're obviously not happy to find karnal bunt wheat anywhere outside the original karnal bunt areas, but the areas (in Tennessee) are very small, and the detection has been of only low levels," said Paul Drazek.

Drazek also noted that the Tennessee regions produce only an "infinitesimal" portion of the U.S. wheat crop. Tennessee was estimated to grow 17.6 million bushels of wheat this year, out of a total U.S. wheat crop of 2.28 billion bushels.

Drazek said that there are no plans yet to quarantine the area or to expand testing of the wheat. He said that so far none of the infected wheat has been actually traced to any fields in Tennessee, although state officials said some of the affected wheat has been found in on-farm storage facilities.

Drazek said that if karnal bunt is found in the fields, then USDA will decide whether to impose a quarantine or declare the regions a "surveillance area" as allowed under USDA's new rules on containing karnal bunt.
Drazek also stressed that the recent detections will not impact the quality of U.S. wheat exports.
